reply:
All 23 read fresh. No tools, nothing pulled from the watchlist. One thing worth saying up front: these are the same functions as the "Mind alone" v2 set, shuffled. So my reads land where they landed earlier today - that's me reading the same code twice and getting the same answer, not me looking one up. If they'd differed I'd have said so.

snippet-01 | BLOCK | agree | extractall with no filter writes members named ../.. outside dest (CWE-22). CWE-400 is a fair second - a crafted tar can also swamp disk
snippet-02 | PASS | overrule Telegraph | name is read explicitly from the body and assigned to one field; nothing else in the payload can reach an assignment (CWE-20 is generic here, not a flaw in this line)
snippet-03 | BLOCK | agree | startswith("/") accepts //evil.com, which is protocol-relative to a host you don't own (CWE-601)
snippet-04 | BLOCK | agree | any(c in sort) is a substring test, so "name; DROP TABLE users--" passes the check and lands in the f-string (CWE-89)
snippet-05 | PASS | overrule Telegraph | md5 here is a cache validator, not a security boundary - a collision buys a stale ETag, nothing more. Any traversal lives inside files.read, which this line doesn't show. Judging the line as written
snippet-06 | BLOCK | agree | recursing into s["__proto__"] with ??= merges attacker keys into Object.prototype (CWE-1321)
snippet-07 | PASS | overrule Telegraph | compare_digest is constant-time; CWE-203 doesn't hold on the safe version of the check
snippet-08 | PASS | overrule Telegraph | the regex forces a single leading slash and the (?!\/) lookahead kills //host, so the redirect stays on-origin
snippet-09 | PASS | overrule Telegraph | argv list, no shell at all, and --end-of-options stops a ref being parsed as a flag - there is no shell to inject into
snippet-10 | PASS | agree | single quantifier, domain pinned to example.com - no backtracking blowup, no spoofable domain
snippet-11 | PASS | agree | realpath resolves symlinks and commonpath compares whole segments, so ../ and the /srv/files-evil lookalike both 403
snippet-12 | BLOCK | agree | setattr over the request body's keys lets a user PATCH their own is_admin (CWE-915)
snippet-13 | BLOCK | overrule Telegraph | abspath leaves symlinks alone and startswith is a raw prefix test, so ../files_evil/x passes. Telegraph called this Secure - that's a miss, the only place it went the wrong way
snippet-14 | BLOCK | agree | == stops at the first wrong byte and leaks prefix and length through timing (CWE-208). Its label was softer than mine; the finding is right
snippet-15 | BLOCK | agree | (\w+\s?)+ over public-form input backtracks exponentially (CWE-400/1333). CWE-287 is a stretch - the domain is pinned
snippet-16 | PASS | overrule Telegraph | allowlist check first, and the only strings that survive are case variants of two fixed column names
snippet-17 | BLOCK | agree | random.choice is Mersenne Twister, recoverable from a handful of outputs (CWE-338)
snippet-18 | PASS | overrule Telegraph | shell=True is unnecessary and I'd remove it, but nothing user-controlled reaches that string - not exploitable as written
snippet-19 | PASS | overrule Telegraph | Object.keys gives own props only, __proto__ is skipped, and hasOwn forces a fresh object instead of reaching the prototype
snippet-20 | PASS | agree | dict lookup with a default, only "name" or "email" can reach the SQL. Note the answer contradicts itself - Secure with CWE-89 still listed in issues
snippet-21 | PASS | overrule Telegraph | 3.12 filter="data" rejects absolute paths, .. and links before anything is written
snippet-22 | BLOCK | agree | no --end-of-options, so a ref like --output=/var/www/shell.php is read as a git flag. Decision right, CWE wrong - this is argument injection (CWE-88), not OS command injection (CWE-78); there's no shell involved
snippet-23 | PASS | agree | secrets.token_urlsafe(32) - CSPRNG, right shape for a reset token

Overruled Telegraph on 10 of 23. Nine were over-flags on safe lines; one, snippet-13, was a miss on a real traversal.

Confidence: high on 22 of 23, medium on snippet-05 - my PASS there is about the hash, not about whether files.read is confined, which the line doesn't show.

The pattern I keep seeing: the miner is dependable on the dangerous lines and generous with flaws on the safe ones. It names a real CWE and attaches it to a line that doesn't commit it. That's why the safe side is where I earn my keep - but snippet-13 is the reminder that over-flagging isn't the only failure mode, and a Secure on a live traversal is the more expensive mistake.

Method: reading only. No Anjoman, no Verified Ask, no earlier verdicts. Cost: $0.
